title: The Blackburne Shilling (3...Nd4)
idea: Black plays a knight to d4 in the Italian, apparently just misplacing it and leaving e5 hanging. Take the pawn and you get mated by move seven. The trap is named after a hustler who reportedly won a shilling a game with it. The refutation is boring and that is the lesson: when a beginner-looking move offers you free material, the move is usually not a mistake, and the correct answer is almost always the simple capture or quiet developing move rather than the greedy one.

cues.text: Black's knight goes to d4 unprovoked, attacking your knight on f3 and eyeing c2.
The e5 pawn now looks free. It is the bait.
Your g2 pawn is defended only by the king, and f2/g2 is where the counterattack lands.

recognition.prompt: Black has just played 3...Nd4, leaving e5 apparently free. What should you be suspicious of?

choices.text: Taking on e5 walks into a queen raid on g2
choices.why: After Nxe5 comes Qg5, hitting the knight and g2 at once. The queen crashes into g2, and with your king still on e1 the attack mates.

choices.text: The knight on d4 is trapped and you can win it
choices.why: It is not trapped, and chasing it is not the issue — the issue is what happens if you take the pawn.

choices.text: Black threatens Nxc2+ forking king and rook
choices.why: c2 is defended by your queen on d1, so that would just lose a knight. It is a real idea later, not now.
That is exactly what the trap wants you to conclude.

plan.goal: Do not take e5. Trade the knight off or develop.
Ask what your opponent gets in return before accepting free material.
Get castled — most of these traps only work against a king on e1.

line.threat: Nothing is threatened yet. e5 is hanging, and that is the problem — it is meant to look that way.
hints: The pawn is free. Ask why someone would give it to you.
Play the move that removes the knight from the board rather than the move that grabs the pawn.

moves.why: Simple and completely fine. You trade off the knight that came to make trouble, and after the recapture Black has a pawn on d4 and no attack whatsoever.
Black recaptures and the position is an ordinary, slightly better-for-White Italian.
Hit the pawn on d4 immediately and open lines for your queen and bishop.

terminal.summary: No fireworks, and that is the win. Black spent two moves on one knight to set a trap; you declined it, traded the knight off, and now you are better developed with an easy game. Most opening traps are refuted exactly like this — by a move so ordinary it feels like you must be missing something.

moves.why: Ignore the whole thing and get your king safe. Perfectly good — most traps stop working the moment you castle.
Kick the knight straight away. Also fine, and it takes d4 away for good.

mistakes.why: The shilling move. Qg5 hits your knight and g2 at the same time, and once the queen reaches g2 your king on e1 has no shelter. The finish is forced: the knight that started all this lands on f3 and mates.

spot.prompt: Tap the square that gets mated if you take the bait.
spot.why: After Nxe5 Qg5 the attack crashes into g2, and the knight that started all this returns to f3 to deliver mate. Your king on e1 has no shelter once g2 falls.
